work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
label: Moses' arms stretched out
def: While Joshua fights Amalek, Moses holds his hands out on the hilltop; Israel wins while they stay up and loses when they drop, so Aaron and Hur hold them up until sunset.
christ: The outstretched arms make the shape of the cross, and the battle is won by the one named Jesus (Joshua): "he who prevailed prevailed by the cross" (Justin, *Dial.* 90). Cyprian reads Amalek as the devil, overcome by Christ (*Test.* 2.16).
where: Justin, *Dial.* 90 — “For if he gave up any part of this sign, which was an imitation of the cross, the people were beaten”
Justin, *Dial.* 111 — “stretching out his hands, remained till evening on the hill, his hands being supported; and this reveals a type of no other thing than of the cross”
Barnabas, *Ep.* 12 — “the Spirit speaks to the heart of Moses, that he should make a figure of the cross, and of Him about to suffer thereon”
Tertullian, *Adv. Jud.* 10 — “the figure of the cross was also necessary, (that figure) through which Jesus was to win the victory?”
Cyprian, *Test.* 2.21 — “By this sign of the cross also Amalek was conquered by Jesus through Moses.”
Cyprian, *Test.* 2.16 — “Amalek was overcome by Jesus, that is, the devil was overcome by Christ.”
